title: November 18 — from learned inquiry to the casino J-lens microscope
summary: Two previously unlisted repositories complete a bridge from controlled active inference to an instrumented frozen Qwen. WonderingQwenSol's learned question-gated GRU retains useful hypotheses; its raw surprise-pull routing fails to help. GamblerQwen exposes Qwen's 12/20/26-layer J-lens concept responses during a hidden-odds reversal, but both free and forced-observation controls mostly select B, so hidden-rule detection is not established.

nodes.claim: WorldLoop 001 tests world-change versus sensor-fault hypotheses and active measurement; 002A/002B train small recurrent question-gated controllers on Bayesian teacher targets, with a separate harder changing-world challenge.
nodes.survived: 001 engineered active policy: 84% full-state accuracy on 200 worlds vs 76% random and 54% repeat vision; no-fault representation 26% on the same evidence. 002A learned GRU reaches 81% vs 29.5% with state reset and 24% separately memoryless. 002B Challenge B: 77–80% four-probe accuracy vs 33.5% state-reset, 44% fixed calibration and 80.5% Bayes. Clamping the question affects actions.
nodes.killed: 001's posterior and information-gain selector are programmed, not Qwen cognition. 002A/002B are small teacher-distilled networks, not frozen Qwen reasoning. The post-hoc 002B surprise-pull ablation matched or improved accuracy (Challenge B 78.5% with surprise off); causal questions are partly structurally imposed. Frozen-Qwen J-lens bridge has fake-model tests but no verified real-model result.

nodes.claim: Offline HTML / CUDA 1.5B Qwen two-armed bandit instrument logs hidden P(A/B), actions, constrained A/B next-token scores and a small-corpus Jacobian-lens read of verbalizable concept directions at layers 12/20/26.
nodes.survived: Two recorded 48-round reversal runs (P(A/B) .76/.24→.24/.76 at round 25) with same underlying latent random draws: real Qwen free-choice records 24 wins and proposes B 45/48; controlled alternating observations record 21 executed wins and Qwen proposes B 47/48. The HTML site replays actual runs and concept traces without inventing feelings or detector confidence.
nodes.killed: No successful rule-change sensing demonstrated. Under forced alternating evidence pre-reversal, A won 8/12 vs B 2/12 but Qwen still proposed B on 23/24 rounds. Its late-layer 'changed' or 'switch' scores drift without matched stationary-world controls; letter bias, prompt length and poor numerical inference remain confounds. Alternating policy rewards are not rewards from Qwen's proposed decisions.

edges.why: GamblerQwen directly reuses Qwenimagination qimag.lens Jacobian code and applies the readout to bandit decision histories.
Sol's independent branch builds active hypotheses and question-gated inquiry to complement externally steered concept loops; Qwen read/write bridge remains unconfirmed.
WaveFormer V2's head-essential recurrent recall motivates persistent latent memory, but WonderingQwenSol uses an independently trained GRU, not a WaveFormer code fork.
Both interrogate frozen-Qwen behavior under changing latent conditions, but GamblerQwen is a separate observation-only instrument and does not use WonderingQwenSol's GRU.

motifs.title: Questions matter only if they alter the selected observation
motifs.description: The teacher-distilled recurrent inquiry controller makes question-conditioned action gating causal; imposed surprise routing did not help, and real Qwen is not yet in this loop.

motifs.title: Reading a concept is not enough to show it controls a choice
motifs.description: A J-lens microscope records gambling-related concept directions during an odds reversal, but Qwen's B preference survives evidence favoring A; detector behavior and causal steering remain open.
